title: Does choiceless polynomial time with counting capture PTIME?
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: Is every isomorphism-invariant polynomial-time property of finite relational structures definable in choiceless polynomial time with counting?
definitions: The input is a finite structure over a fixed finite relational vocabulary, without a supplied linear order. Invariance means that relabeling its elements preserves the property. PTIME is measured on explicit relational encodings; the machine deciding a property may use the encoding order, but its answer must be invariant. The intended choiceless model operates on hereditarily finite sets built from input atoms, with counting and polynomial bounds on the active objects and execution time. No arbitrary selection of a representative from an unordered set is available.

context_blocks.text: Capturing polynomial time without relying on an arbitrary input order is a central problem of descriptive complexity. Choiceless computation is a concrete candidate formalism rather than an unspecified future logic.

Blass, Gurevich and Shelah introduce the model and analyze limits of computation without choices. Adding counting is part of this candidate’s target; negative results for the version without counting do not settle it. Particular graph families likewise do not establish capture on all finite structures.

why: Test a leading concrete candidate for an order-independent characterization of polynomial-time computation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
